# Heredity by discrete factors (Mendel) (`heredity_genetics`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/biology.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Life sciences (`biology`)
- Deps: helped by probability_statistics, selective_breeding, cell_theory, reproduction_fertilisation
- Core idea: Traits are passed on by discrete inherited factors (genes) that come in pairs, one from each parent; they do not blend like paint. One version can hide the other. Cross pure-breeding round-seeded peas with wrinkled-seeded ones: all offspring are round. Let those self-pollinate: the wrinkled form reappears unchanged in one quarter of the next generation, three round to one wrinkled. This needs pure lines, controlled pollination (cut off the anthers, dust with chosen pollen, bag the flower) and hundreds of plants counted. For breeders: a hidden trait can be carried unseen for generations, two parents showing it breed true, and mating close relatives brings hidden defects together.
- Pitfalls:
  - Believing what parents acquire in life (a trained muscle, a docked tail, an injury) is inherited
  - Expecting exact 3 to 1 ratios in small numbers
  - Treating most human traits (height, skin and eye colour, intelligence, character) as single-factor
  - Sliding from heredity to eugenics and the breeding of 'better' people, the historic misuse of this idea
  - Saying Mendel was unread because he was obscure; his paper was distributed and cited, but nobody saw what it meant until 1900
- History: mesopotamia: c. 870 BC – Assyrian reliefs show hand pollination of date palms; practical breeding without theory; greece: c. 400 BC – Hippocratic writers suppose seed is gathered from all parts of both parents' bodies; europe: 1760s – Kölreuter's plant hybrids; 1799 Knight reports crossing pea varieties; 1865 Mendel's lectures in Brünn (printed 1866); 1900 rediscovery by de Vries, Correns and Tschermak; 1902 Boveri (and Sutton in America) link factors to chromosomes; americas: 1910 – Morgan links white eyes in fruit flies to the X chromosome; 1913 Sturtevant maps the relative positions of linked genes
- Read:
  - Gregor Mendel, Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden, Verhandlungen des naturforschenden Vereines in Brünn (1866)
  - Robin Marantz Henig, The Monk in the Garden (2000)
  - Siddhartha Mukherjee, The Gene: An Intimate History (2016)
